correctness.rationale: The stated theorem, as distinct from every inference in the frozen proof, is correct. Let A be intact adjacency, E the deleted-edge toggle and m=N/2. Coordinate flips give A²=(d mod 2)I. If d is even, splitting by a coordinate yields the layer matrix with off-diagonal identity and diagonal A_(d−1), where A_(d−1)²=I. Thus rank A=m. In the bipartite parity block, the deleted endpoints lie outside the totally isotropic images of H and Hᵀ, so the rank-one update raises rank H by one: rank B=m+2. With full endpoint vectors e,f, the four independent vectors e,f,p=Be,q=Bf span W. There Bp=e+q, Bq=f+p; e is cyclic, B³e=f and B⁴e=q=B²e+e. The polynomial is therefore (t²+t+1)², and im B²=W since it lies in W and W is invertible. Rank on the zero summand is m−2, giving only size-two nilpotent blocks. Fixed-space dimensions on W are 0,2,4 at powers 1,3,6 by polynomial gcd; this works whether or not the quadratic splits. At d=2 the zero summand vanishes. If d is odd, H'H'ᵀ=I+L with L=uuᵀ+auᵀ+uaᵀ, a nonzero isotropic and orthogonal to u. L has rank two and L²=(u+a)(u+a)ᵀ is a rank-one projection. Both parity blocks of B² thus have one simple zero, one size-two block at 1, and m−3 simple blocks at 1. B has two simple zero blocks, because a square cannot turn a nonsimple zero block into a single simple zero without increasing its multiplicity, and rank B=N−2. The frozen line 48 list of partitions is not exhaustive from the square and dimension alone (pairs of J₁(1) can replace J₂(1)); close the gap as follows. D=A+I satisfies D²=0, and the coordinate-layer calculation with diagonal A_(d−1)+I gives rank D=m. Therefore im D=ker D=(ker D)⊥. U=span{e,f} intersects ker D trivially: De and Df have nonzero off-endpoint parts on opposite parity sides. Since im E=U, ker(B+I)=ker D∩ker E, of dimension m−2 by independence of the two endpoint constraints on ker D. The frozen witness (B+I)³x=u+c with B(u+c)=c+a≠0 forces a size-four block, since every block at 1 has size at most four by the square. This consumes both size-two blocks of the square; the remaining m−3 blocks at 1 have size at most two and dimension 2(m−3), hence all size two. The odd fixed-space dimensions on the invertible part at powers 1,2,4 are m−2,N−4,N−2. Kernel increments give the stated transient counts; invariant direct sum gives the exact product census, which counts configurations, not cycles. Fresh GF(2) rank tests d=2,…,7 and full state enumerations d=2,3,4 agree, including odd ranks [m+2,4,3,2] for powers 1–4 of B+I.
